steps.text: Combine sugar, flour, and salt together in a medium saucepan. Whisk in eggs and milk; cook mixture over low heat, stirring constantly (and patiently), until mixture has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, up to 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and continue to stir until pudding has cooled slightly; whisk in butter and vanilla until incorporated and smooth.
Spread pudding into a large serving dish; layer with sliced bananas and vanilla wafers.
Chill at least 1 hour in the refrigerator before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Banana Pudding
raw_recipe.description: Make homemade banana pudding from scratch with this easy recipe; layer with vanilla wafers and sliced bananas, then chill for a decadent dessert.

review.reviewBody: I really liked this easy recipe, all the ingredients on hand. The only thing I was disappointed about was the size of the dish I made it in. Be sure to use only an 8x8 or a 8x10 dish. I used a 9x13 dish and the pudding was only about 1/2 inch deep. I was so disappointed. Next time I will just double the recipe for a 9x13. Otherwise, very good.

It tasted really good. I doubled the recipe to put in 2 pie tins. I didn't have the cookies so I made graham cracker crust. I had to add 4 tablespoons of corn starch to get the custard to thicken up. I also increased the temperature on stove top to medium low to speed up the thickening process. I stirred on Low temperature for over an hour before I decided to turn the temperature up. It was quite clumpy when I took it off the heat so I mixed it up with my hand held mixer and then it got creamy. I recommend adding corn starch in with the flour before adding the other ingredients. I would have done it that way to begin with but this was my first time making pudding from scratch. I don't think it would have turned out so good if I didn't use my hand mixer to make it creamy.

Delicious!!! I did tweet it though: used six egg yolks (no whites), used 1.5 heavy whip & .5 half n half (2 cups total). I beat eggs then I slowly added milk to eggs and beat well. I then added that mixture to the dry mixture slowly in med. heat while storing until thick. I did NOT use any butter! I mashed (with a fork) 6 bananas and added them to the mixture. It’s AMAZING!!!!!! We will eat w wafers! I won’t put in, bc they will get mushy!

I used 4 egg yolk instead of 3 eggs. I substituted half the milk for heavy cream (so.. half and half). Everything else I followed. I quadrupled the recipe. It was the best pudding I've ever had. It also tastes better with strawberries than bananas.

The pudding was tasty with 3 whole eggs and was thick in less than 10 minutes. I substituted corn starch for flour and reduced sugar to 1/2 cup. I had lots of soft lady finger cookies and used them instead of vanilla wafers and everything fit nicely in an 8x8 pan. After it chilled I covered with a thin layer of lightly sweetened whipped cream. My guests loved it.
My family loves this recipe. It is clean, timeless, and delicious.
I've made this recipe several times. Each time it's devoured.

The key to this is stirring at almost every step. Whisk dry ingredients in the pan you plan on cooking in, incorporate the beaten eggs with out heat and slowly add the milk once it's mixed then turn on heat. It took 25 min to thicken up but I didn't have lumps like others did and it tasted great and made an even better banana pudding.

So I just finished making ‘this recipe and it is absolutely amazing. However, I did make a few changes: I used 5 egg yolks instead of whole eggs. I know from experience that using whole eggs in custard makes for a bad consistency.
I used 2 cups milk and 1 cup heavy cream. At first I did 1 1/2 cups milk and 1/2 cup cream but realized I would need a bit more pudding, so I added 1/2 cup of each.
I love flavorings and had brandy flavoring on hand as I added 1 tsp brandy flavor and 1 tsp vanilla. Outside of that I kept everything else the same. Here is the finished product.
Good recipe, but whip 2 cups of heavy cream with 1/3 cup of sugar and add to the top.

I mixed everything together in one bowl, except the bananas. I cooked the pudding until it thickened. I let it cool slightly and stirred in two mashed bananas with a little lemon juice. I layered it with Nutter Butter Cookies and sliced bananas. It was perfect for my 9x9 dish. It was easy, so I will definitely make it again soon!
Easy to make, awesome flavor,

My first crack at making a banana pudding from scratch! I was on my toes stirring like crazy as to keep from getting any lumps ...oh well, there were just a few but wow! the pudding came out absolutely delicious! No more instant boxed ...yuk!
I had no problems with this recipe. it turned out as expected and I'm very happy with it. just make sure to follow step by step. I used shortbread cookies instead of the wafers.
Lots of flavor, I cooked it on medium heat almost to a boil, did not like the nilla wafers soggy so next time I won't add them till served.

My pudding never thickened in the fridge. After researching why I discovered it needs to be brought to a boil. All the recipe says is to keep it on low heat until it thickens, which I did. In order to activate the starches it needs to bubble. The recipe should indicate this. You want medium-low heat.

Never made pudding before. This was easy to follow and the ratios are perfect. As a new by, I would just say, keep stirring and don't let it get hot enough to bubble and it really needs to be sticking to the spoon (mine was wooden) and you will be fine! I had to heat mine a second time to get the thickness I wanted and nothing bad happened...lol
Ads jumping around made it more difficult than it needed to be but other than that it was fun.
Well, first off, you never just let banana slices be the last topping and exposed to air, always..and I mean always, let the vanilla wafers be on top on the pudding.
We reduced the sugar, and it was pleasant. As others have said, some extra heat seems to be necessary for the thickening process. Other than that, it was fun to make!
